hook: Two carrion crows just solved a visual test in 235 milliseconds.

sections.voiceover: Two carrion crows just solved a visual test in 235 milliseconds.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a carrion crow's eye looking at a screen.
b_roll: Macro shot of a carrion crow

sections.voiceover: Researchers at the University of Tübingen tested two carrion crows on moving dot patterns. Why do these two carrion crows process visual information twice as fast as human primates?
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing moving dots on a laboratory screen.

sections.voiceover: But researchers Philipp Schmidbauer and Andreas Nieder found they use identical logic despite different brains.
sections.visual_cue: Side-by-side comparison of a human brain and a crow brain silhouette.

sections.voiceover: This University of Tübingen experiment confirms carrion crows process visual data at double human speed. They achieved this 235 millisecond result consistently in the study published on October 22.
sections.visual_cue: Animation showing the dot pattern moving and a timer hitting 235ms.

sections.voiceover: Science proves these two carrion crows possess a reaction speed of only 235 milliseconds.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a carrion crow looking directly into the camera.
